steps: Cook 75g dry rice: simmer in double its volume of salted water, covered, for 15-18 minutes until tender, then fluff.
Brown 150g ground beef in a hot pan over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it cooks, 6-8 minutes until no pink remains; season with salt, pepper and cumin to taste.
Stir in 100g black beans and 50g salsa, and simmer 3-4 minutes to heat through.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or microwave for 20-30 seconds until pliable.
Fill each tortilla with rice, the beef-bean mixture and 30g grated cheddar, then roll into a burrito, tucking in the sides.
Once cooled, wrap the batch portions individually and refrigerate for reheating through the week.
Rinse 100g rice (or half rice, half quinoa) and simmer in salted water for 15-18 minutes until tender, then fluff.
Warm 200g black beans through in a small pan with a splash of water, 3-4 minutes.
Warm 80g corn through in the same pan, or dry-toast it in a hot pan for a little char.
Divide the rice between bowls and top with the black beans, corn, 80g guacamole and 60g salsa.
Finish with hot sauce to taste and serve.
Preheat the oven to 220°C (425°F).

In a bowl, combine 200g diced sweet potato, 150g crumbled tofu (press it between kitchen towels under a heavy weight for 15-20 minutes first to remove excess water), 1 tbsp chipotle in adobo and a little oil; mix well.
Spread onto a foil-lined baking sheet and bake for 15 minutes, flip with a spatula, then bake a further 5-10 minutes until the sweet potato is cooked through and the tofu starts to brown.
Meanwhile, warm 100g black beans through in a small pan.
Mash ¼ avocado with a squeeze of lime juice.
Warm the corn tortillas, then fill each with the sweet potato and tofu mixture, black beans and mashed avocado; serve with extra lime, salsa or hot sauce.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add 100g ground beef with a pinch of salt and cook, breaking it into bite-size pieces, about 3 minutes until lightly browned.
Finely dice ½ carrot, 1 stalk celery and ¼ onion, add to the pot and cook, stirring occasionally, about 5 minutes until softened.
Pour in a splash of red wine and let it bubble for 1 minute to cook off the alcohol.
Add 200g crushed tomatoes, bring to the boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, about 25 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Taste and add more salt and pepper if needed.
Meanwhile, cook 120g pasta in salted boiling water until al dente; drain and serve topped with the bolognese.
Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil and cook 110g pasta according to packet instructions until al dente; drain, reserving a splash of cooking water.
Meanwhile, heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a pan over medium heat, slice 100g mushrooms and fry for 5-6 minutes until browned.
Add 2 cloves minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in 150g cooked brown lentils and 200ml passata, and simmer for 8-10 minutes until the sauce thickens, loosening with reserved pasta water if needed.
Toss the drained pasta through the sauce, tear over basil, and serve.
Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F).
Thinly slice ¼ courgette into ribbons and wilt 50g spinach in a dry pan for 1-2 minutes; set both aside.
Mix 150g marinara with 60g cooked lentils to make a bolognese-style sauce.
In a baking dish, layer lasagne sheets, the lentil-marinara sauce, 80g cashew ricotta, courgette and spinach; repeat the layers, finishing with sauce on top.
Cover with foil and bake for 35-40 minutes until the pasta is tender, then uncover and bake a further 10 minutes to brown the top.
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing into 6 portions.
Bring a pot of salted water to the boil and cook 120g pasta until al dente; drain, reserving a splash of the cooking water.
Season 150g chicken breast and grill or pan-fry over medium-high heat, 5-6 minutes per side until cooked through; rest for a few minutes, then slice.
Halve 100g cherry tomatoes and warm through in the pasta pot for 1-2 minutes.
Toss the drained pasta with 30g pesto, loosening with the reserved cooking water, then fold through the tomatoes.
Top with the sliced chicken and 15g grated parmesan to serve.
Peel and dice 200g butternut squash, then boil or steam for 10-12 minutes until fork-tender.
Meanwhile, cook 110g GF pasta in salted water according to packet instructions; drain, reserving 100ml of the cooking water.
Blend the cooked squash with 1 tbsp olive oil, the minced garlic clove, 2 tbsp nutritional yeast and enough reserved pasta water until smooth and creamy.
Warm 100g white beans through in a small pan.
Toss the pasta through the squash sauce, fold in the white beans, and season with salt and pepper to serve.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok or large frying pan over high heat.
Beat 2 eggs and pour in, scrambling briefly until just set, then push to one side of the pan.
Add the minced garlic and 100g carrot, peas and scallion, and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until just tender.
Add 300g day-old rice, breaking up any clumps, and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until heated through and starting to catch at the edges.
Add 80g diced ham or chicken if using, then stir in 1½ tbsp soy sauce and toss everything together for 1 minute.
Fold the scrambled egg back through and serve immediately.
Press 200g tofu to remove excess water, then cut into small cubes.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and fry the tofu for 4-5 minutes until golden on most sides; remove and set aside.
Add 150g peas and carrots to the wok and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until just tender.
Add 300g day-old rice, breaking up any clumps, and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until hot.
Return the tofu to the wok, add 2 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tsp sesame oil, and toss to coat.
Scatter with sliced scallions and serve.
Soak 100g rice noodles in hot water for 5-8 minutes until softened, then drain.
Cube 200g tempeh and pan-fry in a little oil over medium-high heat, 4-5 minutes per side until golden.
Add minced garlic and ginger to the pan and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add 200g broccoli, carrot and snap peas, and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until just tender-crisp.
Toss in the drained noodles and 2 tbsp tamari, and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until everything is combined and heated through.
Rinse 100g jasmine rice and cook according to packet instructions; keep warm.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry 180g beef strips in batches, 2-3 minutes until browned; remove and set aside.
Add minced garlic and ginger to the wok and cook for 30 seconds, then add 200g broccoli, carrot and snap peas, and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Return the beef to the wok, add 3 tbsp coconut aminos, and toss everything together for 1-2 minutes.
Serve over the jasmine rice.
Rinse 90g rice and cook according to packet instructions.
Heat oil in a pan, add minced garlic and ginger and cook for 30 seconds, then add 200g mixed stir-fry vegetables and stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until tender-crisp; stir in 1 tbsp soy sauce.
Bring a small pan of water to a gentle simmer, crack in 2 eggs and poach for 3 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still soft.
Serve the rice topped with the stir-fried vegetables, poached eggs and sliced ½ avocado.
Soak 150g rice noodles in hot water for 5-8 minutes until softened, then drain.
Slice 150g chicken breast thinly and stir-fry in a little oil over high heat, 4-5 minutes until cooked through.
Add sliced ginger and 100g peeled courgette and carrot, and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until just tender (peeling keeps the fibre low for race week).
Toss in the drained noodles, 2 tbsp tamari and 1 tsp sesame oil, and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until combined and hot.
Serve immediately.
